The profile header, in every state the live data actually has

Six specimens. Each is a real title, byline or tag combination from aikyamfellows.org. The rule under test is the same in all six — and the states with no pipe need no special case at all.

What a build has to get right

Split the title on |. Trim both halves. Never split on :. If there is no pipe, render one span and stop. Never render a placeholder for a missing standfirst — four live profiles have none. Never render a placeholder for a missing portrait.

Two authors is the common case, not the exception: most pieces are bylined to a person plus “aikyam fellows”. ⚠️ Whether that organisation credit is real or an import artefact is the one question here that needs someone with Ghost access — and it changes every byline on the site.

State 1 · the happy path

Pipe with spaces both sides, a standfirst, one author, two topics.

Sentinaro Shiu A Heart that Listens

Sometimes, the people who change lives are simply the ones who know how to listen.

By Aparna R · 3 August 2026

Education Mental Health

State 2 · no space before the pipe

The live title is literally Rahul Thomas| Theatre Saved Me. A typo at source, and it will not be the last one. The trim absorbs it and the rendered result is identical to State 1. ⛔ A splitter that does not trim leaves a leading space in the phrase. Fix the title in Ghost as well — the layout surviving a typo is not a reason to keep it.

Rahul Thomas Theatre Saved Me

What happens when you walk away from a secure career to follow your calling?

By Aparna R · 25 July 2026

Art & Culture

State 3 · no pipe, no standfirst, two authors

A bare name. No editorial phrase exists and no intro sentence exists. Four live profiles are like this. ⛔ No placeholder, no invented subtitle, no “Read her story”. The phrase slot is simply absent — [data-headline-phrase]:empty removes itself, with no branch in any template — and the byline moves up.

Ramya Sundararajan

By Haneen Naseer with aikyam fellows · 3 December 2025

Aftercare Education

State 4 · a colon, and the name in the middle

⛔ This is why the rule is “split on | only, never on :”. A splitter that treated the colon the same way would set “The Bauls & Millet Songs” as a person's name at 42px, on a page about Shilanjani Bhattacharyya. Rendered whole, in ink, long and correct. text-wrap: balance does the work.

The Bauls & Millet Songs: Shilanjani Bhattacharyya’s Journey

By Haneen Naseer with aikyam fellows · 3 March 2026

Art & Culture

State 5 · the portrait, and what sits near it

The full header with the photograph in place, at its own aspect ratio, full-bleed on a phone. ⭐ No text sits on it and no scrim touches it. The caption names the person — an uncaptioned portrait on a site whose whole subject is people is the page failing at its own job.

Rahitha Krishnadas Beating Barriers

She was told the Chenda wasn’t for girls. From challenging tradition to inspiring women.

By Aparna R · 21 July 2026

Art & Culture

State 6 · no portrait — ⚠️ UNVERIFIED

A profile with no photograph. ⚠️ This state could not be confirmed to exist. It is here because a site with dozens of profiles and a decade ahead of it will have one, not because one was found. Two minutes with the repository confirms or deletes this specimen.

⛔ No grey silhouette, no initials avatar, no stock image. A generic body-shape where a person should be is worse than nothing — it says the site has someone and simply did not bother. The figure is omitted entirely and the prose begins after the topics.

Jasentha Joy Pickles and Chuckles

By Haneen Naseer with aikyam fellows · 5 May 2026
